textbookText: Fig 2.5.3 Reproduction in Marchantia by Gemma 2. Sexual Reproduction Marchantia is dioecious. The sex organs are developed on special stalked receptacles called gametophores. The gametophore bearing male sex organ (i.e. antheridium) is called antheridiophore while the gametophore bearing female sex organ (i.e. archegonium) is called archegoniophore. Antheridiophore has an erect about 2-3 cm long stalk. The top of antheridiophore flattened , slightly curved, 8-lobed disc, known as male receptacle. Each lobed disc consist of antheridial chambers and air chambers alternately. Each antheridial chamber consists of antheridium which is attached to the base by short multicellular stalk. Each antheridium consists of single layered oval body and a stalk. Inside the oval body, there is mass of androcytes which later develop into motile, biflagellated antherozoids (i.e. male gametes). After maturation, the antheridial wall absorbs water, ruptures and biflagellated antherozoids are liberated out into water.

Archegoniophore consists of long stalk and 8-lobed, umbrella shaped, female receptacles. Each receptacle consists of nine fingers like structure called rays. Female sex organs occur on ventral surface of lobes. Each patch contain 12-16 hanging archegonia. All archegonia are covered by protective layer called perichaetium or involucre. A mature archegonium is flask shaped structure with swollen base, venter and a long narrow, neck. Venter contains a large egg (oosphere) and a venter canal cell. Neck consists of 4-6 neck canal cells. The tip of archegonium is protected by four cover cells or lid cells.

(a) Figure 2.5.5 (a) L.S. of Archegonium (b) Archegonium In a fully mature archegonium, the neck canal cells and venter canal cell disorganize to from mucilage mass which absorbs water and swells up. It creates a pressure, results in the separation of cover cells. The passage is formed upto egg. Fertilization takes place in the presence of water. The antherozoids liberated from antheridium, swim through water and are attracted towards archegonium. Although many antherozoids enter the archegonium, only one fuses with the egg to form zygote. The zygote represents the first stage of sporophytic generation. Zygote divides repeatedly to form embryo and embryo gives rise to multicellular sporophyte inside the venter of archegonium. Sporophyte is completely parasitic over gametophyte since it fully depends on Biology, Grade 11 | 125

gametophyte for their nutrition. A mature sporophyte is differentiated into foot, seta and capsule. A foot is basal part, attached to the receptacle and absorbs nutrition from the gametophyte. Seta is short stalk that connects foot and capsule. The capsule is oval structure with single layer of jacket that encloses number of fertile spore mother cells and sterile elater mother cells. Each spore mother cell undergoes meiosis and forms four haploid spores. Some elater mother cells provide nutrients to the spore mother cells in early stage while some elater mother cells form elongated, narrow, spindle shaped structures called elaters. On maturation, the capsule wall ruptures and spores are dispersed with the help of elaters. The spores germinate to develop new gametophyte under favourable condition.
